latin: Pharmacopōlae, antequam<sup>1</sup> mūnere suō fungī possent, jūsjūrandum ōlim dare dēbēbant. Ecce exemplar hujus jūris jūrandī<sup>2</sup>:
«... habēbunt pondera vēra et jūsta ā lībrā<sup>3</sup> usque ad scrūpulum.
Nōn pōnent in suīs clisteribus<sup>4</sup> aliquam medicīnam cujus virtūs<sup>5</sup> sit exhālāta vel corrupta<sup>6</sup>.
Nōn pōnent ūnam medicīnam prō aliā in aliquā receptā<sup>7</sup>...
et sī herbam vel medicīnam in recepta positam nōn habeant, referent magistrō ōrdinantī ut circā<sup>8</sup> hōc prōvideat.
Nōn dabunt nec permittent darī scienter aliquod<sup>9</sup> clistērium nec aliquod aliud medicābile...
nisi ad hōc habeant receptam ab aliquō magistrō speciāliter ōrdinātam.
Nōn recipient clēricum<sup>10</sup> nisi sciat intellegere, loquī et scrībere latīnum et gallicum<sup>11</sup>...
et antequam ipsum recipiant, tenēbitur jūrāre omnia praedicta jūrāmenta.
Parīsiīs, diē 2° mēnsis octōbris, annō 1422°.»
latinAccented: Pharmacopṓlae, ántequam<sup>1</sup> mū́nere suō fungī possent, jūsjūrándum ōlim dare dēbḗbant. Ecce exémplar hujus jūris jūrándī<sup>2</sup>:
«... habḗbunt póndera vēra et jūsta ā lībrā<sup>3</sup> usque ad scrū́pulum.
Nōn pōnent in suīs clistéribus<sup>4</sup> áliquam medicī́nam cujus virtūs<sup>5</sup> sit exhālā́ta vel corrúpta<sup>6</sup>.
Nōn pōnent ūnam medicī́nam prō áliā in áliquā recéptā<sup>7</sup>...
et sī herbam vel medicī́nam in recépta pósitam nōn hábeant, réferent magístrō ōrdinántī ut circā<sup>8</sup> hōc prōvídeat.
Nōn dabunt nec permíttent darī sciénter áliquod<sup>9</sup> clistḗrium nec áliquod áliud medicā́bile...
nisi ad hōc hábeant recéptam ab áliquō magístrō speciā́liter ōrdinā́tam.
Nōn recípient clḗricum<sup>10</sup> nisi sciat intellégere, loquī et scrī́bere latī́num et gállicum<sup>11</sup>...
et ántequam ipsum recípiant, tenḗbitur jūrā́re ómnia praedícta jūrāménta.
Parī́siīs, diē 2° mēnsis octṓbris, annō 1422°.»
english: Pharmacists, [before being able to carry out] (before they might acquit themselves of) their function, formerly had to take an oath. Here is a reproduction of this oath:
“... they will have true and accurate weights from the pound to the «scruple».
They will not put in their enemas any (some) medicine whose strength has evaporated or [is] corrupted.
They will not put [one single] medicine for another in [any] (some) prescription...
and if they do not have (subj.) the herb or the medicine [prescribed] (placed) in the prescription, they will refer [to the doctor] (master) prescribing, so that he may take measures on this subject.
They will not knowingly give or allow to give any enema, nor any other medicine...
if they do not have (subj.) a prescription specially prescribed (ordinatam) on this subject (ad hoc) by a [doctor] (master).
They will not accept any [assistant] (clerk) if he does not know (subj.) how to understand, speak and write Latin and French...
and before [admitting] (they receive) [this] (him) [assistant], [the latter] will be bound to swear all the aforesaid oaths.
Paris, 2 October 1422.”

footnotes: Antequam is construed with the INDICATIVE if it simply indicates that, of two events, one is prior to the other, and with the SUBJUNCTIVE if there is reason to highlight an intention, a hypothesis, etc. (whence possent, subj. impf.).
Jus, juris, n., right (legal)... or juice, sauce! Jurandus, -a, -um, verbal adj. of jurare; juramentum (plural below, P. 9) is less classical than jusjurandum (gen. jurisjurandi).
Libra, -ae, f., 1 pound (weight) = 12 ounces = 288 scruples; uncia, -ae, f., ounce (weight), or inch = 1/12 of a foot (length); scrupulum = 1/288 of a pound or of a foot.
Clister, -eris, m., or clisterium, -i, n.: barbarous device used to give enemas (also written clyster, pronounce clustèr).
Corrumpere = cum + rumpere. Rumpo, -is, -ere, rupi, ruptum, to break.
Receptus, -a, -um: perfect participle of recipere, to receive, = re + capere. Used here in a sense that corresponds fairly well to that of its French derivative recette (recipe).
Circa: prep. + acc., towards, around, on the subject of (here a doubtful use).
Aliquis, qua, quod, adj. indefinite pronoun, some, a certain.

Here is a more correct form for sentence 8: non accipient adjutorem nisi latine et gallice intellegere, loqui, scribere possit (accipient, recipient: future indicative). Likewise, in sentence 9, tenebitur jurare is not classical; it would be better to say: (totum) jusjurandum supradictum dare debebit.
comments: Phrase 3: simple succession of facts, so antequam + ind. — Pyxis, -idis, f., the box. — Jaceo, -es, -ere, jacui, v. i., to be lying; not to be confused with jacio, -is, -ere, jeci, jactum, v. t., to throw. — Peniculus, -i, m., brush; penicillus, -i, m., paintbrush. Note the expression vel minima, even the slightest, and more generally vel + superlative (of the adjective or adverb); vel optime, even the best possible. Vel used as a conjunction means or (not exclusive) whereas aut corresponds to or exclusive.

latin: Avē, Domne pharmacopōla (vel domna pharmacopōla), estne tibi remedium ad pītuītam cūrandam aptum?
Ecce! Guttās decem ex hāc ampullā māne, merīdiē et vespere in nāsum īnstillā!
Antequam cubitum abeās, pilulās duās ex illā pyxide cum pōtiōne calidā sorbe.
Volō unguentum quoque contrā sōlis exustiōnēs.
Sī hōc unguentō cutem ūnxerīs, sōlis exustiō nunquam nocēbit.
Ita nōn arbitror, cutis mea vel minimā exustiōne statim vulnerātur.
Tunc cave sōlem; nōlī in arēnā tōtō tempore postmerīdiānō jacēre.
Cōnsiliō tuō ūtar... Dentifricium etiam volō... quid amplius? certus sum mē alicujus reī oblītum esse.
Vīsne sāpōnem ad barbam rādendam?
Nēquāquam! Novācula ūtor electrīcā... Ēia! Invenī! Pēniculum dentārium volō.
latinAccented: Avē, Domne pharmacopṓla (vel domna pharmacopṓla), estne tibi remédium ad pītuī́tam cūrándam aptum?
Ecce! Guttās decem ex hāc ampúllā māne, merī́diē et véspere in nāsum īnstíllā!
Ántequam cúbitum ábeās, pílulās duās ex illā pýxide cum pōtiṓne cálidā sorbe.
Volō unguéntum quoque contrā sōlis exustiṓnēs.
Sī hōc unguéntō cutem ū́nxerīs, sōlis exústiō nunquam nocḗbit.
Ita nōn árbitror, cutis mea vel mínimā exustiṓne statim vulnerā́tur.
Tunc cave sōlem; nōlī in arḗnā tōtō témpore postmerīdiā́nō jacḗre.
Cōnsíliō tuō ūtar... Dentifrícium étiam volō... quid ámplius? certus sum mē alicújus reī oblī́tum esse.
Vīsne sāpṓnem ad barbam rādéndam?
Nēquā́quam! Novā́cula ūtor electrī́cā... Ḗia! Ínvenī! Pēnículum dentā́rium volō.
english: Hello Mr Pharmacist (or Mrs Pharmacist), do you have a remedy for treating a [head cold] (pituitary)?
There you are! Put (instil) ten drops from this bottle in your nose morning, noon and evening.
Before going to bed [take] two pills from this box with a hot drink (absorb).
I also want a cream against [sunburn] (burns of the sun).
If you [rub] (fut. ant.) your skin with this cream, you [will never have] sunburn (sunburn will never harm).
I [don't think so] (thus), my skin is sensitive to the slightest burn (immediately is wounded).
Then, be careful of the sun; please don't stay lying all [afternoon] (afternoon time) on [the beach] (the sand).
I [will follow] (will make use of) your advice... I also want toothpaste... What else? I'm sure I've forgotten something.
Do you want shaving soap (soap for shaving the beard)?
Not at all! I use an electric razor. Ah! I've found it! I want a toothbrush.
